findings.title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
findings.body: Cancelling now only sets `cancelled: true`. The actual SendGrid cancel waits for the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron, which runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before a reminder's `scheduledDate` (e.g. due in 5 minutes), SendGrid sends the email before the cron gets to it. The old code cancelled immediately, so this is a regression for near-term reminders. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the cron window should be cancelled immediately.

findings.title: Reschedule and workflow/step deletion still cancel immediately, hitting the 100 pending-cancellation limit
findings.body: The PR says the root cause is SendGrid's cap of 100 pending scheduled_send cancellations. Yet several paths pass `immediateDelete=true`, which issues the `scheduled_sends` cancel right away: rescheduling here, plus workflow deletion and step deletion in workflows.tsx. Deleting a workflow with many future reminders, or many reschedules, still fills the cancellation quota. Further cancellations then fail silently (only logged) and emails go out anyway, so the bug is only partially fixed.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel blocks all later cancellations on every run
findings.body: All cancellations run sequentially inside a single try/catch. If `client.request` throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, quota error, etc.), the loop aborts. The remaining reminders are not cancelled, and the already-queued deletes are never awaited. The failing reminder stays `cancelled: true` and is retried first on every run, so it can block the others until their emails are sent. Each reminder needs its own try/catch.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are fire-and-forget
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called inside `forEach` without awaiting. The handler returns before the DB update (`cancelled: true`), the row delete, or the Twilio cancel completes. In a serverless environment the function can be frozen before these finish, so reminders stay un-cancelled and are still sent. The old code at least awaited the DB deletes. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking.ts and workflows.tsx.

findings.title: Unawaited reminder deletion races with step deletion cascade
findings.body: For a deleted step, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` start without being awaited, and then `workflowStep.delete` runs. Step deletion cascades to the reminders, so the concurrent `workflowReminder.delete` / `update` calls can hit already-deleted rows and throw (only logged). The Twilio and SendGrid cancel may also not complete before the response is returned.
